topic: Compile-Time Polymorphism via Specialization and Recursion
explanation: This focuses on how template metaprogramming, specifically using template specialization and recursion, allows for compile-time polymorphism, drastically impacting code generation and runtime performance.  Unlike runtime polymorphism (virtual functions), template metaprogramming performs all the type-specific computations during compilation. This eliminates the runtime overhead of virtual function calls but introduces increased compile times and potentially larger binary sizes for a wider range of template instantiations. The compiler generates distinct, optimized code for each specific type used with the template, potentially leading to better performance but demanding significant compiler resources.
keywords: Static Polymorphism, Template Metaprogramming, Compile-Time Polymorphism, Template Specialization
